issues.description: Inconsistent getter name for the ingredient's name between template and solution. The template repository's StockIngredient defines getIngredientName() and Stock.findStockIngredient() calls getIngredientName(), whereas the solution repository uses getName() and Stock.findStockIngredient() calls getName(). This discrepancy in method naming across artifacts may confuse students about the expected getter name for the ingredient name and lead to mismatched references when comparing examples or implementing related code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the getter name for the ingredient's name consistent across template, solution, and documentation. Either rename the template methods to getName() and adjust references, or update the solution and any examples to use getIngredientName(). Also clarify the expected getter naming in the problem statement (e.g., specify getName()) so students are not uncertain which convention to follow.

issues.description: The accessor for the StockIngredient.name field is named getIngredientName() in the template code but getName() in the solution. The problem statement asks students to 'add getters for all the private fields' but does not mandate the exact getter name. However, the differing getter identifier across template and solution creates a mapping friction: students reading the solution or tests may be confused which getter to use and why two different names refer to the same concept (the ingredient's name).
issues.suggestedFix: Standardize the getter name for the StockIngredient.name field across all artifacts. Prefer using getName() (to match the common convention and Meal.getName()) in both template and solution, and update all calls (e.g., in Stock.findStockIngredient) to use getName().
